purpose: LiDAR cross-check of the F015 camera-yaw hypothesis; refutes it (see F017).
extrinsic: Table 3 OS1-16: identity rotation (0,0,0,1) + translation (-0.098, 0.000, 1.000) m; base_link at ground level
method: Ouster /os_cloud_node/points (32768 pts, synchronized) -> parse PC2 x/y/z -> transform to base_link -> trunk-height band (0.2<Z<1.2 m, 1<X<8 m, |Y|<2.6 m) -> cluster L/R -> robust line fit per side -> centreline slope = LiDAR heading. Camera heading = mean line-fit heading across all 9 CP-5 models.
conclusion: LiDAR (identity extrinsic) measures ~+3.84 deg row tilt vs base_link, agreeing in sign and magnitude with the camera (~+3.25 deg). A camera-specific mount yaw (F015) would require LiDAR ~0 deg; it is not. Tilt is sensor-common -> base_link-vs-row geometric offset (mechanism open, F017).
caveats: LiDAR extrinsic nominal (Table 3); small LiDAR-frame yaw not fully excludable but cannot produce ~+3.8 deg from an expected ~0 deg.
6 anchor frames selected toward high-tilt scenes (camera ~3.25 deg here vs ~2.28 deg val-mean); direction/agreement conclusion robust to selection.
